name: @examples/dev-harness
//dependencies: The harness is a workspace dependency because this example *is* its end-to-end case:
`vp dev` here runs the real plugin against a real `forguncy.config.ts`, which is what makes
it evidence rather than an illustration.
`@forguncy-react-workspace/runtime` is the façade the Cell's authored source imports by name.
It is a *source* dependency rather than a deployed module: the compiler flattens it into the
artifact like any other source file (#14), and the dev server resolves it as source through
this workspace link. Its being flattened per Cell is also what makes the façade's single
`@forguncy-react-workspace/core` is not a dependency: nothing in `src/` imports it, and the
config file's `defineForguncyConfig` is the only use — which arrives through the workspace
root's resolution. Nothing in the Cell's own module graph reaches `core`, which is the point
of the Cell's source importing only the façade.
`react` is deliberately NOT a dependency, for the rule `examples/host-antd/package.json`
records at length: `react` is decided `host`, the bridge intercepts the specifier before node
resolution, and installing it would be a silent escape hatch for a broken interception. Under
`vp dev` the harness supplies the substitution from its own pinned dependency instead, which
is the arrangement that keeps this example's `package.json` honest about what the page owns.
//scripts: `vp run dev` is the local loop for this example, and the `--configLoader runner` flag is not
optional — it is the difference between a working harness and a config that cannot load.
Vite's default config loader (`bundle`) externalizes every import in `vite.config.ts` that
resolves into node_modules, and this repository's workspace packages are *source*: they are
linked into node_modules but their `exports` point at `.ts` files with extensionless relative
imports. A bundled-then-node-loaded config therefore dies with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot
find module .../packages/core/src/ownership`, because node ESM requires the extension and the
config bundler deliberately did not rewrite it.
`runner` loads the config through Vite's own module runner instead, so the same resolution the
rest of the toolchain uses applies to the config file too. Verified both ways on a real dev
server: plain `vp dev` fails with that ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, `vp run dev` serves the Cell.
This is a script rather than a bare `vp dev` because Vite reads `configLoader` *before* it can
read the config file, so it cannot be set from inside `vite.config.ts` — and `vp dev` is a
built-in command that a `package.json` script cannot override. `vp run dev` is Vite+'s own
documented way to reach a project's dev script; see its guide, 'Built-in Commands vs Scripts'.
//devDependencies: `@forguncy-react-workspace/core` is a devDependency rather than a dependency because its only
use is `defineForguncyConfig` in the committed config, which Vite loads itself. The Cell's
module graph never reaches it — asserted in the example's own test, which checks that the
compiled artifact carries no copy of it.
